title: Privacy policy
intro: Redline is a car-spotting sticker album. It is built so that other people are protected too: the owners of the cars you photograph and the people around them.
summary_body: Licence plates are blurred on your phone before anything is uploaded. Plate text and GPS coordinates are never stored. Co-Driver AI is optional and can be switched off at any time. You can delete your account and everything in it yourself.
controller_body: Redline is a student project of Jasper Degreef for the Mobile Applications course at UCLL (Leuven, Belgium). He is the controller of the personal data described here.
data_body: Your account (email address and username). Your spots: the blurred photo, the car, its paint and body style, the city name, the date, your notes, whether Co-Driver helped and a short fingerprint of the photo to warn you about duplicates. For cars you register as an owner: make and model, nickname, a one-way hash of the plate, its last two characters, your visibility choice and the sightings of that car.
never_body: The original, unblurred photo. The text of licence plates (a plate you type is used once to find a verified owner and then thrown away). GPS coordinates or exact places: the city is worked out on your phone and only its name is saved. Photo metadata (EXIF): every photo is re-encoded on your phone first.
purposes_body: To run your sticker album and progress, to let Co-Driver fill in a spot when you choose to use it, to notify verified owners that their car was spotted, and to keep the service safe (rate limits against abuse).
legal_basis_body: Performance of the contract when you create an account and use the album (GDPR article 6.1.b). Your consent for Co-Driver AI and for sharing your username with owners, which you can withdraw in the Trust Center at any time (article 6.1.a). Our legitimate interest in preventing abuse, and the legitimate interest of car owners and passers-by in not being identifiable (article 6.1.f).
retention_body: Your account, spots and photos: until you delete them or your account. Sightings: until the spot, the car or one of the accounts is deleted. Rate-limit counters: at most two days. Settings and the offline copy of your album stay on your device until you log out.
processors_body: Supabase (database, login and photo storage, hosted in the EU in Frankfurt). Vercel (hosting of the web app). Cloudflare Workers AI (Co-Driver recognition: the photo is processed without being stored, zero data retention). Mistral AI (EU) only if it is configured as the fallback for Co-Driver.
ai_body: With Co-Driver on, a smaller copy of your photo (at most 768 pixels, without metadata) is sent through our server function to the AI provider. It returns the car, the colour and where the plates are. Its answer is only a suggestion: you confirm every plate yourself. Co-Driver can be used 15 times a day. With Co-Driver off, no photo is sent for recognition at all.
owners_body: Only owners whose ownership is verified receive sightings. A sighting shows the car, the city, an hour window and the blurred photo. It never shows your notes, the exact time, other spots or your account, and your username only if you chose to share it. One spotter pings the same car at most once a day.
rights_body: You can see, correct and delete your data in the app: delete a spot, a car or your whole account (Me → Delete my account). You also have the right to access, portability, restriction and objection, and you can complain to the Belgian Data Protection Authority (dataprotectionauthority.be).
children_body: Redline is meant for people aged 14 and older. In Belgium, the digital age of consent is 13.
security_body: All traffic is encrypted (HTTPS). Every table is protected by row-level security, plates are compared as salted hashes in the database, and the web app sends a strict content security policy.
contact_body: Questions or requests: Jasper Degreef, through github.com/ShadowFlashy/mobile-application (open an issue, or ask for a private contact address there).
